In this method, spectrum sensing is executed, post which secondary users are assigned to the idle bands present, in a sequential manner. There is no provision to accommodate multiple users as well as to consider variable data rates, which limits the efficiency of the system. Another concern is the effect of Adjacent Channel Interference (ACI). ACI refers to the phenomenon of faulty filters degrading the efficiency of adjacent filters. There are no proposed systems to eradicate this. Hence, to maximize the efficiency of the Cognitive Radio system, along with a provision to eliminate ACI, we propose the Multiple User Variable Rate Guard Band-Aware Assignment (MUVR-GB Aware) Method. The MUVR is a smart method to improve spectrum efficiency with instantaneously allocating channels to several CR transmissions at different time slots by considering channel-dependent achieved transmission rates. This scheme enables the accommodation of multiple users in a single spectrum, based on the data rates required, which results in high system efficiency. The addition of Guard Bands is to make sure ACI has no adverse effects on the spectrum. It has been observed post simulations, that the MUVR-GB Aware assignment exhibits minimum wastage of the spectrum along with maximum secondary user accommodation, as compared to the existing Sequential Assignment.

Author Keywords: Multiple User Variable Rate-Guard Band Aware

articleTitle: Influence of Age and Gender on Pedestrian Rule Compliance and Crossing Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: To successfully navigate roads, autonomous cars must understand the behaviors of individuals of different ages and genders. It is crucial to thoroughly comprehend pedestrians' vulnerabilities and risky choices to ensure their safety. This paper focuses on pedestrian behavior, particularly regarding street crossings and compliance with rules among pedestrians of various ages and genders at both signalized and unsignalized crossings. To evaluate how pedestrian demographics influence rule compliance and crossing decisions, video-based observation is utilized. The study found that older adults and seniors tend to break laws more frequently than younger adults. Moreover, although women generally adhere to laws more than men, the difference between genders is not substantial. However, the activities, walking speeds, and decision-making processes of older and very young pedestrians make them more prone to accidents.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Applications in Banking for Credit Rating and Risk Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: In the intricate world of financial services, the adjudication of loan applications stands as a critical determinant of an institution's fiscal health and risk exposure. Conventional methodologies, reliant on manual vetting and subjective appraisal, are increasingly at odds with the industry's shift towards data-driven and customer-centric approaches. In response to this challenge, our research offers a novel paradigm: the application of sophisticated machine learning (ML) algorithms to transform the traditional loan assessment process into an automated, precise, and efficient system. We conduct an extensive evaluation of various ML models, including but not limited to ensemble techniques and neural networks, to forecast loan repayment probabilities. The LightGBM Classifier emerges as the paramount choice, with an exemplary accuracy rate of 96.6%, due to its effective handling of large datasets and resistance to overfitting. Critical to our approach is the emphasis on minimizing false negatives—erroneously predicting high-risk loans as low-risk—which carries substantial financial implications. To this end, we employ the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve and the Area Under the Curve (AUC) analysis to meticulously calibrate the decision threshold. Our empirical analysis showcases the potency of our selected model, buttressed by ROC and AUC, to reduce false negatives and thereby fortify the loan approval process against potential defaults. This paper extends beyond a mere presentation of ML efficacy; it illustrates a roadmap for integrating these computational techniques into the operational fabric of financial institutions. The resulting benefits are multifaceted: elevated processing speed, scalability to accommodate growing data volumes, and a marked improvement in customer experience due to faster decision times. Our study's implications resonate with the broader theme of digital transformation in finance, delineating a future where ML algorithms are not auxiliary but integral to the decision-making ecosystem of lending operations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach to Road Surface Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: Potholes are the most serious threats to road safety and maintenance. They lead to enhanced accidents, damage to vehicles, and huge monetary losses because of inefficiencies in transportation. It's time to deal with this as part of enhancing road infrastructure and protecting the public. The aim of the paper will be to introduce a highly advanced deep learning-based system for detecting potholes in roads through user input as images or even videos and discuss its user- friendliness, speed, and accuracy. The web interface will enable users to upload an images or videos, view results, and receive an alert indicating it is a “Pothole” or “Normal Road.” One remarkable ability of the system is calculating distance from the camera to the pothole so that maintenance teams can act promptly. These developments reduce maintenance costs while improving road safety through prompt repair. It uses YOLOv8 as a preprocessing technique to enhance the images and videos by eradicating segmentation noise and resizing, with the aid of object detection using YOLOv4 and MobileNetV3. The dataset is divided into the training and test subset for effective accuracy regarding detection, using a combination of CNN and MobileNetV3. The performance was tested by using performance metrics like accuracy, SSIM (Structural Similarity Index Measure), and PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio). My contribution was that the CNN mechanism for the classification part, combined with YOLO for detection, rendered the classical method significantly more potent regarding pothole detection. Future work would be in streamlining the real-time processing capabilities and simply making the user interface even more accessible and efficient.

articleTitle: Smartguard: An IoT-Enabled Real-Time Monitoring System for Urban Manhole Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: The proposed system is a revolutionary low-cost long-term solution for manhole safety, provided with IoT monitoring. The features of subterranean drainage conditions are unpredictable, and this prevents human inspection systems from being reliable. Smartguard overcomes these challenges by utilizing an extensive wireless sensor network and IoT monitoring technologies combined with a real-time monitoring framework. The sensors are employed alongside GSM and Wi-Fi modules to provide a separation-based approach solution that enables the secure long-distance transition of the data to the central station. The software is based on Twilio and SMTP and provides the data processing and the resultant email and SMS alerts in LSTM networks are designed for the predictive analytics. As the current study indicates, the accuracy of identifying gas leaks, water levels, and obstructions is, in general, significantly high. The increase amounts to 95, 93, and 96%, respectively. Similarly, false alarms are also decreased as well as the response rate when compared to the existing systems. Thus, Smartguard is an important solution in the overall assessment of urban infrastructure management, as it guarantees improved sustainability, operational efficiency, and safety.

articleTitle: From Words to Faces: Automated Suspect Image Synthesis and Retrieval from Criminal Databases
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: Forensic technology has greatly changed the nature of suspect identification, which plays a critical role in public safety and the delivery of justice. Traditional artist-drawn sketches are highly skill-based, time-consuming, and tend to result in different renderings that may lead to inaccurate depictions of the suspect. Existing approaches also often lack the integration of modern database capabilities, limiting the ability to rapidly cross-reference criminal records. This paper proposes a novel architecture to directly generate suspect images from eyewitness descriptions based on the Stable Diffusion Model. Through an intuitive form, the eyewitness would be able to generate a preliminary image of the suspect and iteratively improve the resemblance by adjusting the salient facial features. A unique feedback mechanism in place allows for iterative improvement that increases the reliability of the generated image. Once finalized, the suspect images are matched against the criminal databases using an optimized FAISS-implemented HNSW indexing for rapid and efficient search. Additionally, our framework provides a “Wanted” poster generation feature that applies disguises to suspect images, assisting law enforcement in the distribution and use of suspect images more effectively in investigations. This comprehensive approach, combining generative models with powerful database search and distribution mechanisms, marks a significant advancement in forensic image synthesis and retrieval.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Authenticate Texture of Cotton and Silk Saree Using Image Processing & RCNN Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: The popularity of sarees, as Indian traditional garment, is spreading all over the world, and because of their variety and different type of materials used in making traditional garment need to automate and classification methods are required to identify best among the existing. This work offers a novel method for classifying and detecting saree types using computer vision techniques. The visual features of sarees are classified by using image processing with machine learning models as preprocessing to improve the classification model. With the use of region based CNNs texture feature will be extracted and identification of different types of material used (Silk/Cotton/Shiffon). The provided material and its category plays a vital role in differentiating Kanchivaram Silk Sarees. The model ensures stability across datasets and training conditions, as demonstrated by experimental findings that show its improved accuracy and speed over using traditional deep learning techniques. This research increases computer vision in apparel recognition and categorization with applications in e-commerce and fashion recommendation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Routing Efficiency in MANETs: Integrating PSO-Optimized Neural Network Model for Improved Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: Because node mobility and network topology changes are dynamic, effective routing is still a major difficulty in the quickly developing field of Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs). This research presents a unique approach to improve routing efficiency in MANETs by utilizing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in conjunction with neural network models. The core of the proposed approach involves optimizing a neural network using PSO to predict the most effective routing paths for data transmission. By integrating evolutionary optimization techniques with advanced neural network models, the system processes various network parameters-such as node distances, energy levels, and statistical metrics-to determine optimal routing paths. Comparative analysis of the PSO-optimized neural network (PSO-NN) and a traditional neural network (NN) model demonstrates that PSO-NN offers superior routing predictions, leading to improved network performance. The findings open the door for further developments in network optimization techniques and highlight how well PSO and neural networks work together to manage the complexity of dynamic network settings.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Circularly Polarized Crossed Dipole Antenna with High Input Impedance Using Artificial Magnetic Conductor for Sub 6ghz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: Design focused on crossed dipole antenna with metallic reflector placed around 0.25 from the radiator. Frequency range of the metallic reflector maintains a phase of +90 to -90. AMC (Artificial magnetic conductor) simulation can be done using unit cell analysis there are 3 layers i.e., Square patch on the top, Substrate in the middle, metal plate in the bottom. Rogers material 5880 with dielectric constant (r)=2.2, per-meability(µr)=1,loss tangent=0.0009,thickness=3.15mm,operating frequency may be in the range of 4.5 to 6.This antenna is used for gain enhancement.

Author Keywords: Artificial Magnetic Conductor,High Input Impe-Dence,Circularly Polarized,Crossed Dipole Antenna

articleTitle: Placement and Interconnectivity in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: Performance and efficiency of Wireless Sensor Networks are significantly impacted by sensor placement and network connectivity. Proper sensor deployment within a target area directly affects the operational efficiency of network, coverage, along with overall performance. Additionally, a well-organized interconnection scheme is essential for smooth communication between sensor nodes and the base station (sink). This paper offers an in-depth review of the challenges related to placement and connectivity in wireless sensor networks, focusing on the latest advancements in sensor technologies and network design. It explores various algorithms and strategies for optimal sensor placement, including deterministic, heuristic, and optimization-based approaches. Furthermore, the paper discusses connectivity solutions such as multi-hop communication, relay node deployment, and innovative techniques for network restoration and coverage enhancement. By analyzing current research and experimental results, this review highlights the trade-offs and benefits of different methods across various wireless sensor network applications, including terrestrial, underwater, and multimedia networks. The insights provided aim to guide future research and practical implementations in wireless sensor network design, ensuring improved network performance and reliability.

articleTitle: State-of-the-Art Computational Intelligence Praxis for Research on Seismic Activity
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: In structural engineering, prioritizing the resilience and safety of buildings and infrastructure in regions susceptible to earthquakes is crucial. This article offers a comprehensive overview of diverse methodologies in structural analysis and seismic design, encompassing various algorithms, machine learning models, and optimization techniques. It covers topics such as artificial neural networks, metaheuristic algorithms, and decision trees. The applications range from earthquake resilience and optimized design to seismic tremor de-clustering. Performance metrics like Mean Square Error and accuracy percentages are consistently used to assess effectiveness. This compilation underscores the versatility of these methods in addressing challenges and optimizing structural designs.

articleTitle: Soft Computing and Machine Learning Approaches for Mapping in an Indian Coastal City for Flood Vulnerability
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping is vital in mitigating flood risks and managing disaster preparedness. This research article proposes a hybrid machine learning model that combines Support Vector Machines (SVM) with Genetic Algorithm (GA) metaheuristic algorithm for making of a Flood Susceptibility Map (FSM) for Chennai city. The objective is to enhance the performance of machine learning in predicting flood-prone areas. Future research directions are suggested, and an analysis is done on the use of such machine learning models in mapping and assessing flood risk. Based on fifteen Flood Conditioning Factors (FCFs), the flood susceptibility model was built. The data from the flood inventory is then split into two categories: 70% is used to train the model and 30% is used to validate it. The accuracy of the generated model is obtained as 80%.

articleTitle: Enhanced Plant Disease Detection in Precision Agriculture Using Autoencoder and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: Agricultural productivity faces significant threats from plant diseases, leading to substantial economic losses and worsening global food insecurity. These diseases can drastically reduce crop yields, adversely affecting farmers' livelihoods and disrupting food supply chains. In response, agrotechnology and precision farming have emerged as critical solutions, emphasizing the need for sustainable crop management through accurate and timely disease detection. Early intervention is essential to minimize disease spread and enhance understanding of crop health. This study presents a comprehensive approach to plant disease classification using a combination of autoencoders for dimensionality reduction and a fine-tuned ResNet-9 architecture. The proposed methodology leverages the autoencoder to effectively reduce the dimensionality of leaf imagery data, thereby simplifying the feature space and improving computational efficiency. The reduced features are then fed into a ResNet-9 model, which has been fine-tuned to achieve high classification accuracy for various plant diseases. Our model achieves a remarkable accuracy of 99.2%. The development of this robust tool aims to facilitate early disease detection and improve crop management, contributing significantly to the field of precision agriculture. By providing precise and timely diagnoses ofplant health, deep learning models hold the potential to revolutionize agricultural practices, thereby enhancing yield and sustainability in food production.

articleTitle: A Concise Review on Machine Learning Based Students’ Academic Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Electronics and Communication System (AICECS)
abstract: Evaluating students' academic performance is an essential activity for any educational institution and one of the major criteria used to rate educational institutions. In the pres-ence of a huge volume of educational information, the task of accurate evaluation becomes more challenging. However, recent emerging technologies, such as machine learning, have made handling this challenge easier. These technologies require the development of effective and efficient machine learning models, either by designing new algorithms or improving existing ones. The current study aimed to analyze various existing studies con-ducted by different researchers on evaluating students' aca-demic performance. This study provided insights into the algorithms, approaches, and datasets used by different researchers. The information presented in this study may help researchers develop models for the precise evaluation of the performance of the students.
